steps.desc: Patients see a certificate warning on the clinic portal, and staff are telling them to click through. Work out what is wrong and fix it safely.
steps.intro: Heads up, this one is a live incident. The clinic’s patient portal is throwing certificate warnings. Take it step by step and work the problem.

alerts.msg: Patients say the portal shows “Your connection is not private”.
TLS certificate for portal.clinic.example expired 2 days ago.
I told everyone to click “Advanced → Proceed” so they can still log in.
Is it safe to type my health details? My browser keeps warning me.

levels.label: High
levels.desc: Sensitive data at real risk right now

tips.start: Read every alert before you decide. Severity is about impact, not panic.
tips.all_in: All alerts are in. What severity is this?
tips.good: Exactly. Now let’s find out why.

good.title: Good call: High
good.text: No breach is confirmed, but patients are typing health data past a warning. That needs action now.

bad.title: Not quite: it’s High
bad.text: Patient data is at real risk right now, but there’s no confirmed breach yet. That makes it High.

steps.title: Inspect the evidence. Tap the 3 clues.

tips.start: Certificates tell a story. Which details explain the warning, and why it keeps getting worse?
tips.progress: Good. Keep reading line by line.
tips.good: That’s the whole story. Now decide what to do.
tips.bad: Look at the dashed ones. Those were the clues.

good.title: Case cracked!
good.text: Expired certificate, auto-renewal off, and staff training patients to ignore warnings.

bad.title: Not quite
bad.text: The clues were the expiry date, disabled auto-renewal and the staff note.

options: Keep telling patients to click through until the certificate is renewed.
Stop the click-through advice, post a maintenance notice, and renew the certificate.
Switch the portal to plain HTTP so the warning disappears.
Leave it until after opening hours. It’s only a warning.

tips.start: You know what’s wrong. What’s the first thing you do?
tips.ready: Sure about that one? Hit Check.
tips.good: Exactly. Stop the harm, then fix the cause.
tips.bad: Not that one. Think about who is at risk right now.

good.title: Contained!
good.text: Stop the harm first, then fix the cause. Patients stop sending data past a broken lock.

bad.title: Not quite
bad.text: Contain first: stop the click-through advice, post a notice, then renew the certificate.

steps.title: Put the response plan in order

items.text: Turn on auto-renewal and expiry alerts
Confirm the portal loads with no warning
Post a maintenance notice on the portal

tips.start: Contain first, then fix, then verify, then prevent. Tap steps in the order you’d do them.
tips.progress: Keep going. Tap a placed step to undo it.
tips.bad: Close. The orange steps are in the wrong spot.

good.title: Incident closed!
good.text: Contain, fix, verify, prevent. The portal is safe for patients again.

bad.title: Not quite
bad.text: Right order: stop the advice, post a notice, renew, verify, then turn on auto-renewal.

debrief.headline: Incident resolved!
debrief.sub: The portal is back on a valid certificate and patients are no longer told to ignore warnings.

meta.description: Triage a live incident, find the evidence, choose the first move and order the response.
